backlog.spec: In train(), after the loader produces an augmented batch (inputs are normalized half tensors of shape (B,C,32,32)), zero a random 8x8 square per image with probability 0.5 using a torch.rand-based mask built like batch_flip_lr (compiled helper, no new imports). Leave everything else unchanged. Expect a small regularization gain; if the epoch budget is too short to benefit, the cost is near zero because the mask is cheap.
backlog.title: Cutout patch after normalization

backlog.spec: Replace the epoch-alternating flip in CifarLoader.__iter__ with an independent per-sample flip each epoch: call batch_flip_lr on the whole augmented batch inside the loop before yielding, and drop the epoch%2 flip branch. Keep the pre-flipped cache removed accordingly. Tests whether per-sample randomness beats the every-other-epoch scheme at this short schedule.
backlog.title: Random per-sample horizontal flip instead of alternating epochs

backlog.spec: Set TRANSLATE to 4 (pad 4 with reflect, random crop back to 32x32) so each image can shift up to 4 pixels; the crop helper already supports any r because it computes r=(H_padded-crop_size)//2. Predict-time TTA in infer() currently hard-codes pad=1 and crops at 0:32 and 2:34; leave that as is. Tests stronger translation augmentation.
backlog.title: Larger translation pad with reflect padding

backlog.spec: In train(), for the first ~40% of steps downsample each augmented batch to 24x24 with F.interpolate(mode='bilinear', antialias=True), then use full 32x32 for the rest. The network is fully convolutional up to the final MaxPool2d(3) which assumes a 3x3 map, so instead keep the spatial path at 32 by only using the downscaled batch for the first phase with an added adaptive pool so the head still sees 256 features. Keep the compiled forward_step with dynamic=False by compiling a second graph for the low-res shape. Goal: fewer FLOPs early on for the same epoch count.
backlog.title: Progressive resolution during training

backlog.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of the trainable conv and head weights (decay around 0.99 per step, started at 60% of total steps) inside train(), using torch._foreach_lerp_ on a list of detached copies. At the end of train(), copy the EMA weights into the model parameters before returning. Since predict() must not change the model, do the copy inside train() only. Targets a small accuracy gain from weight averaging when the LR is already near zero.
backlog.title: Weight EMA over the final part of training

backlog.spec: Make Muon's momentum ramp from 0.85 at step 0 to MUON_MOMENTUM=0.655 would be the wrong direction, so instead ramp it from 0.5 at step 0 up to 0.75 by the 30% mark of total steps and hold there. Implement by updating group['momentum'] each step inside the training loop from step/total_train_steps, next to the existing lr updates. Tests whether early low momentum helps the orthogonalised updates settle.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup

backlog.spec: Set nesterov=False in the Muon construction inside train() (the Muon class already supports the flag and then uses the raw momentum buffer for orthogonalisation). Keep all other hyperparameters identical. This is a structural optimizer switch that may trade a little convergence for a simpler update path.
backlog.title: Nesterov off for Muon

backlog.spec: In _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, increase the number of unrolled quintic iterations from 3 to 5 by repeating the three-line block (A = X @ X.transpose(1,2); B = b*A + c*(A@A); X = a*X + B@X) two more times. Keep fullgraph=True. Expected effect: closer-to-orthogonal updates per step at a modest extra matmul cost on the small convolution filters.
backlog.title: More Newton-Schulz iterations for Muon

backlog.spec: The head weight is a 2D matrix of shape (10,256) and currently uses Nesterov SGD. Move model.head.weight into the Muon parameter group by handling 2D params in the Muon path: pass it to Muon separately and reshape within the existing 4D-only filter list by adding a branch that treats 2D tensors as (D,K) with no reshape. Keep the head LR at HEAD_LR scale multiplied by the existing factor. Tests whether orthogonalised updates help the classifier layer.
backlog.title: Use Muon for the head as well

backlog.spec: Replace the linear decay to zero for Muon's lr with a shape that holds the LR at its initial value for the first 20% of steps and then decays linearly to 0 by the end. Implement by changing the lr_factor2 expression in the training loop only for optimizer2's group. Keeps the bias and head schedules unchanged. Tests whether a flat-then-decay schedule suits the orthogonalised updates better.
backlog.title: Separate LR schedule shape for the Muon group

backlog.spec: Replace the linear decay of lr_factor1 (whiten bias and norm biases) and lr_factor2 (head) with a cosine factor 0.5*(1+cos(pi*progress)) where progress = step/total_train_steps, keeping the same starting LRs. Muon keeps its linear decay. Tests whether the SGD-driven parameters prefer a smoother tail.
backlog.title: Cosine-shaped decay for bias and head groups

backlog.spec: Add a linear warmup over the first 3% of total steps that multiplies every param group's LR by step/(0.03*total_train_steps) until it reaches 1, and then continue with the existing linear-to-zero decay. Implement in the training loop by multiplying lr_factor1 and lr_factor2 by min(1, step/warm_steps). Tests whether a brief warmup stabilises the first Muon steps with the high initial target magnitude.
backlog.title: Short learning-rate warmup for all groups

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE to 2048 and scale BIAS_LR, HEAD_LR and MUON_LR by sqrt(2048/1536) (about 1.15) so the per-step update magnitude stays comparable. The number of steps drops by about a quarter at the same EPOCHS, which lowers time per epoch through better GPU utilisation. Weight decay is already scaled by batch size inside train(). Tests the speed-accuracy tradeoff on the batch axis.
backlog.title: Batch size 2048 with scaled learning rates

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE to 1024 and scale BIAS_LR, HEAD_LR and MUON_LR by sqrt(1024/1536) (about 0.82). This increases the number of optimizer steps for the same epochs, which often helps accuracy on small networks at the cost of more Python and optimizer overhead per epoch. Tests the other side of the batch axis.
backlog.title: Batch size 1024 with scaled learning rates

backlog.spec: Replace the per-step Python loop that writes group['lr'] with tensor-valued learning rates held in a single torch tensor on the GPU: compute lr_factor1 and lr_factor2 as 0-dim CUDA tensors updated with fill_ once per step, and pass them as the lr to the fused SGD and to the Muon step via group['lr'] tensors. Reduces host overhead between steps. Behaviour should be identical; the goal is pure wall-clock reduction.
backlog.title: Gradient accumulation free: fewer Python-side LR updates

backlog.spec: Change the forward_step compile mode from max-autotune to reduce-overhead so the forward and backward graphs are captured as CUDA graphs, keeping fullgraph=True and whiten_bias_grad as a Python bool (two graphs). Compilation is untimed, so the only effect is per-step launch overhead. Check that the loss tensor is cloned before the next step to avoid overwritten CUDA graph outputs.
backlog.title: Use CUDA graphs for the training forward-backward

backlog.spec: Remove the whiten bias from the optimizer entirely (do not add it to param_configs) and always pass whiten_bias_grad=False into the model, so the whitening bias stays at its initialised value of zero. This removes one parameter group and the branch in forward. Tests whether the 0.2-epoch whiten bias training contributes measurable accuracy.
backlog.title: Drop the whitening bias update after the first phase by freezing it

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup, change nn.SiLU() to nn.ReLU(inplace=False) for both activations, leaving the initial GELU in CifarNet.layers unchanged. ReLU is cheaper than SiLU in both forward and backward and the batch norm before each activation keeps the scale stable. Tests whether the speed gain outweighs any accuracy loss.
backlog.title: Replace SiLU with ReLU in the conv groups

backlog.spec: Change widths in CifarNet from block1=64, block2=256, block3=256 to block1=64, block2=192, block3=256 (or the equivalent reduction in block2 only). The second block dominates FLOPs at 16x16 resolution, so reducing it cuts time roughly in proportion. Keep the head input size consistent with block3. Tests the time-accuracy frontier along the width axis.
backlog.title: Lighter middle block width

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup.forward, after conv2 and norm2 but before the final activation, add the input to the group's pooled output x_pool (the tensor after pool, before norm1) when the channel counts match. Only block2 and block3 match shapes with their conv2 output if the channel counts are equal, so apply the skip only when channels_in == channels_out (block3 input is 256, output 256). Adds almost no compute. Tests whether a residual path helps the deeper block.
backlog.title: Residual skip inside the second conv of each group

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup, replace nn.MaxPool2d(2) with nn.AvgPool2d(2) and the final nn.MaxPool2d(3) in CifarNet.layers with nn.AvgPool2d(3). Average pooling smooths the features and may generalise differently with the SiLU activations and the scaled head. Keep all other code the same. Tests whether the pooling choice matters at this scale.
backlog.title: Average pooling in place of max pooling

backlog.spec: Make the label smoothing value a function of progress inside train(): start at LABEL_SMOOTHING=0.09 and linearly decay to 0 by the final step. Since forward_step currently closes over a constant, pass the smoothing value as a Python float argument to forward_step and let torch.compile recompile for a varying float, or instead blend the loss manually: loss = (1-s)*CE_hard + s*CE_uniform with s updated per step. Tests whether regularisation is most useful early.
backlog.title: Label smoothing that decays to zero

backlog.spec: With probability 0.25 per batch, replace the batch with a convex mix of itself and a shuffled copy (lambda drawn from Beta(0.4,0.4) via torch.distributions or a sigmoid of a uniform sample) and train on the mixed cross-entropy. Keep label smoothing. This is a regularizer for longer runs; at this short schedule it may hurt, so measure against the baseline.
backlog.title: Mixed-batch label smoothing with a small mixup component

backlog.spec: Set the color_jitter enabled flag to False in train()'s aug dict so only flip and translate remain. Removes the batch_color_jitter op from each epoch. The jitter magnitudes were tuned but its removal is a clean ablation that measures how much regularization the photometric augmentation contributes at 7.65 epochs.
backlog.title: Brightness and contrast jitter off

backlog.spec: In train(), change the whitening covariance estimate from train_loader.normalize(train_loader.images[:960]) to the first 5000 images (or all 50000 if fast enough). The covariance is computed from training images only, so this is allowed under the harness rules provided it is computed inside train() and not cached across runs. Expect a slightly better whitening basis at small extra cost in the timed run.
backlog.title: Whitening init from more training images

backlog.spec: In predict(), switch infer() to tta_level=1 (horizontal mirror only, which uses the existing infer_mirror path on all images) instead of tta_level=2. This drops the shifted-crop views and the uncertainty selection, lowering predict time. Measure whether the accuracy drop is smaller than the time saving in the cost formula (1 percent of time is about 0.01 in ln cost).
backlog.title: Prediction with fewer TTA views to save time

backlog.spec: In infer()'s tta path, add two more shifted views (offsets (0,2) and (2,0) in addition to the current top-left and bottom-right crops, from a reflect-pad of 1 pixel) so each uncertain image is averaged over more views before flipping. Keep the 25 percent uncertainty selection. Tests whether extra test-time views buy accuracy cheaply, since predict time is small relative to training.
backlog.title: Wider prediction TTA: five shifts with flips

backlog.spec: During train(), at the end of each of the last 3 epochs, store a detached copy of the model's parameters. In predict(), average the logits of the final model with logits from the stored snapshots. Since predict must not change the model, implement the snapshot forward passes with torch.func.functional_call or by temporarily loading each snapshot into a cloned model stored in train()'s scope. Tests whether a cheap logit ensemble recovers accuracy near the end of the linear decay.
backlog.title: Snapshot ensemble of logits over the last epochs

backlog.spec: In CifarNet.__init__, change whiten_kernel_size from 2 to 3. Set whiten_width = 2 * 3 * whiten_kernel_size**2 (so 54 channels instead of 24). Spatial sizes become 30, 15, 7, 3 and the final nn.MaxPool2d(3) still reduces the 3x3 map to 1x1, so no other shape changes are needed. init_whiten already takes h and w from the weight shape, so it adapts automatically. Keep Muon's max_D and max_K computation as it is. Everything else stays fixed.
backlog.title: Whitening kernel size 3

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup.forward, move the pooling so that it runs after conv2 and before norm2, instead of after conv1. The order becomes conv1 -> norm1 -> activ -> conv2 -> pool -> norm2 -> activ. Pooling after the wider conv keeps more of the channel information before downsampling. Keep the 2x2 MaxPool. The spatial sizes at each block stay the same, so the head and the final MaxPool2d(3) are unchanged. This is one structural edit and needs no hyperparameter change.
backlog.title: Max pool after the second conv in each group

backlog.spec: Add nn.Dropout2d-style channel dropout to the features before the head. In CifarNet.forward, after self.layers, apply F.dropout with p=0.05 to the (N, 256, 1, 1) pooled features, but only while self.training is True. Implement it as a module attribute such as self.drop = nn.Dropout(0.05) created in __init__ and called in forward. Keep the head scaling by 1/x.size(-1) unchanged. Predict runs in eval mode, so no change is needed in predict.
backlog.title: Channel dropout before the head

backlog.spec: In train(), use loss reduction='none' in forward_step so that per-sample losses are returned. Keep a per-sample running loss tensor of length N, and update it from each batch's detached losses, indexed by the batch indices. From the second half of training, skip the 25 percent of samples with the lowest recent loss on each epoch (choose the kept set once at the start of each epoch from the stored losses, then shuffle the kept indices). Scale the loss so the gradient magnitude per step stays close to the current scale, by dividing by the mean over the kept batch size. Keep the stored-loss buffer as a per-run tensor created inside train(), so no state leaks between runs. The total number of steps must still match total_train_steps, so compute it from the kept count.
backlog.title: Dynamic pruning of the easiest samples in later epochs

backlog.spec: Replace the linear decay factors lr_factor1 and lr_factor2 in train() with a shape that stays at 1.0 for the first 40 percent of total steps and then decays linearly to 0 at total_train_steps. Concretely, define frac = step / total_train_steps and factor = 1.0 if frac < 0.4 else (1 - frac) / 0.6. Use this factor for optimizer2 (Muon) and the head group. For the whiten-bias and norm-bias group keep the existing whiten_bias schedule. The Muon target magnitude schedule inside _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5 is unchanged. Only the LR multiplier shape changes.
backlog.title: Flat-then-decay global LR schedule

backlog.spec: Change the linear decay of all learning-rate multipliers so they decay to 0.1 of their initial value instead of 0. In train(), replace lr_factor1 = 1 - step * lr_factor1_base with lr_factor1 = 1 - 0.9 * step * lr_factor1_base, and similarly for lr_factor2 = 1 - 0.9 * step * lr_factor2_base. Keep the same base step counts. The floor keeps the final updates from vanishing, which may help the averaged test predictions. This is a one-line change to each factor, plus the matching change in the Muon target-magnitude end value if needed (leave it unchanged for the first run).
backlog.title: Nonzero LR floor at the end of training

backlog.spec: At the end of train(), before returning, recompute BatchNorm running statistics on clean data. Set each BatchNorm module's momentum to None (cumulative average), reset its running stats with reset_running_stats(), and run the model in train mode under torch.no_grad() on the un-augmented, un-flipped normalized training images in batches of 2000, using the same forward path as training. Then restore momentum to 1 - 0.5566 and switch back to eval. The statistics then match the unaugmented test distribution rather than the running averages collected under flip, shift and jitter. Do not change predict(), which must not modify the model. This runs only inside train() and uses images from the current run, so the reuse rule holds.
backlog.title: Recalibrate BatchNorm statistics after training

backlog.spec: In infer(), inside the tta function and the _get_tta_logits helper, change the aggregation so that the softmax of each view is averaged instead of the raw logits. Specifically, in _get_tta_logits replace averaged_logits = reshaped_logits.mean(dim=0) with averaged_logits = torch.log(reshaped_logits.softmax(dim=-1).mean(dim=0) + 1e-12). Keep the view construction unchanged. The argmax of the output is then the argmax of the mean probability. The log keeps the output as logits of the expected form. Do not change the uncertainty selection, which still uses initial_logits. This is a small change to the prediction function only.
backlog.title: Probability averaging in test-time augmentation

backlog.spec: In _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, remove one of the three Newton-Schulz blocks, so only two iterations run (the A, B, X update block appears twice instead of three times). This makes the Muon step cheaper. Because the orthogonalization is less exact, keep the a, b, c coefficients as they are first and rely on the existing norm scaling and target magnitude to hold the update size. This is a speed-oriented change that trades a little orthogonality for time. The step count, batch size and all other settings stay the same.
backlog.title: Two Newton-Schulz iterations for Muon

backlog.spec: Add a lookahead wrapper around the Muon group. Keep a slow copy of each filter parameter, created inside train() after init_whiten, and every 6 optimizer steps interpolate the slow weights toward the fast weights with slow = slow + 0.5 * (fast - slow), then copy slow back into the fast parameters. Only the convolution filters in filter_params are affected. Reset the slow copies to the current weights at the start of every run inside train(), so nothing carries between runs. The final model weights used by predict are the slow weights after the last synchronization. The slow-copy buffers must be freed at the end of train() so host and device memory do not grow across runs.
backlog.title: Lookahead slow weights on the convolution filters

backlog.spec: In forward_step, replace the plain label-smoothed cross-entropy with a focal-style weighting. Compute per-sample losses with reduction='none' using the same label smoothing. Multiply each by (1 - p_true)^gamma, where p_true is the softmax probability of the target class, detached from the graph, and gamma = 0.5. Sum the weighted losses as before so the LR scale is unchanged. This down-weights samples the network already classifies confidently and leaves the rest of the script untouched.
backlog.title: Focal-weighted cross-entropy

backlog.spec: Start training at batch size 768 and grow it linearly to 2048 over the run, rounding each step's batch to a multiple of 256. Keep the total number of samples seen per epoch fixed. Scale the learning rates of all groups by sqrt(batch / 1536) at each step, so the effective LR tracks the batch size. Use a per-step index slice on the shuffled permutation instead of the fixed-size loader. Keep the number of optimizer steps about equal to the baseline. The only change is the batch schedule.
backlog.title: Batch-size ramp during training

backlog.spec: The head currently returns self.head(x) / x.size(-1), a fixed scale. Replace that constant with a learnable scalar parameter, initialised to 1/x.size(-1) and trained with the head's Nesterov SGD group and no weight decay. The head weight is still re-normalised in reset(). This lets the network learn its own logit temperature, which interacts with label smoothing. Keep the parameter in fp32 or half as the rest of the head is, and make sure it is reset in reset() so every run starts from the same init.
backlog.title: Learnable head output scale

backlog.spec: In Muon.step, the gradient-norm rescaling is applied only every norm_freq steps, and norm_freq grows from 2 to 17 over training. Set the rescaling to run on every step (norm_freq fixed at 1) and keep the rest of the update as is. This removes the staleness of the cached scale factors late in training, when the gradient norms change quickly. The compute cost is one extra foreach norm per step, which is small next to Newton-Schulz.
backlog.title: Muon gradient-norm rescale every step

backlog.spec: Replace the single linear decay with a two-phase schedule. Phase one decays the LR for all groups linearly from the initial value to 0.35 times the initial value at 60 percent of total steps. Phase two jumps back to 0.5 times the initial value and decays linearly to zero at the final step. Apply the same multiplier to Muon and to the SGD groups. The total number of steps and the final LR are unchanged, so the run time is unchanged. This is a single warm restart in the style of SGDR.
backlog.title: Warm-restart learning-rate schedule

backlog.spec: In predict, before running inference, switch the BatchNorm layers to use the statistics of the current prediction batch instead of running statistics. Do this without changing the stored running buffers, so the model is not modified. Run each 2000-image chunk in train mode under torch.no_grad() with momentum set to 0, then restore eval mode. Because the test set is treated as one distribution, this corrects any shift between the training running stats and the test distribution. Apply it to the basic view only, and keep the TTA views on the same path. Check that predict still returns logits of shape (N, 10).
backlog.title: Transductive BatchNorm at prediction time

backlog.spec: In the first ConvGroup, replace the max-pooling layer after conv1 with a stride-2 convolution. Keep conv1 as a 3x3 kernel with padding 1 and add a 2x2 learned downsample conv with stride 2 after the whitening layer instead. Alternatively, make conv1 itself stride 2 with a 3x3 kernel, which halves the number of positions for conv2 and keeps the output shape the same. Keep the same widths, the batch norm, and the SiLU. Note that the output size after the three blocks must stay 4x4 before the final 3x3 pool, so verify the shapes.
backlog.title: Stride-2 convolution in place of the first max pool

backlog.spec: Add a per-batch scale augmentation after the crop. For each batch, draw a scale factor s uniformly from 0.9 to 1.1. Resize the 32x32 batch with bilinear interpolation to round(32*s) pixels, then center-crop or reflect-pad back to 32x32. Apply it with probability 0.5 per batch. Compile the helper with torch.compile as the other augmentations are, and make sure the output shape is always 32x32 so the training loop does not change. This adds a mild zoom augmentation alongside the translation.
backlog.title: Random scale jitter by interpolation

backlog.spec: In Muon's update, scale the learning rate of each filter by a factor depending on its reshaped matrix. Multiply the step for each parameter by sqrt(max(1, D / K)), where D is the reshaped output dimension and K the input dimension. This is the common Muon scaling that matches the update RMS across layers of different aspect ratio. The base MUON_LR stays as is, but the first conv of block one has a very different aspect ratio than the others. Implement it by building a per-parameter multiplier once in the constructor and applying it in the foreach update.
backlog.title: Shape-aware Muon learning-rate scaling

backlog.spec: Change the color jitter so that brightness and contrast are drawn independently for each colour channel rather than once per image. In batch_color_jitter, sample a brightness shift and a contrast scale of shape (B, 3, 1, 1) instead of (B, 1, 1, 1), with the same ranges as now. Apply them as before. This adds colour-balance variation that the global jitter does not produce. The compute cost is unchanged. Keep the same enable flag and ranges so the comparison isolates this change.
backlog.title: Per-channel brightness and contrast jitter

incumbent.description: Progressive resolution: for the first 40% of steps, bilinear-antialias downsample each augmented batch to 24x24 and compile the training step statically (dynamic=False), with the final MaxPool2d(3) swapped for AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) so both resolutions feed the head 256 features.

memo:
Incumbent is now slot 17, progressive resolution (first 40% of steps downsampled): official -0.1896/-0.1322, mean adjusted -0.1547 over 2 runs. It was flagged "tripwire", so audit or replicate it before building on it. The earlier "no change helped" note is outdated.

Helped: data-side speed changes (progressive resolution).

Neutral within noise (sd about 0.026): colour jitter off (-0.0058 official), extra TTA views (+0.0072 delta), softmax-averaged TTA (-0.0092 delta, rejected).

Hurt: larger batch (+0.0571), narrower middle block (+0.1090), pad 4 (+0.0945), floored LR decay (+0.3154), head on Muon (+4.6760), BN recompute (+0.0358), per-channel jitter (+0.0490), per-sample flip (+0.0814).

Crashes: slots 2, 3, 13, 14, all architecture or BN/head edits. Avoid them.

Next: resolve the tripwire first. Then tune progressive resolution (fraction of steps, start resolution), and try fewer TTA views to save time. Keep slots in reserve for replicates.
